summary: mock-datas-lib conceals obfuscated payload in database.js and executes it via Function constructor on library use
details: Package advertised as a mock-data generator ships an obfuscated loader in index.js and an encoded payload in database.js disguised as a product catalog. The exported getTransactions API invokes load_transaction_data, which iterates records in database.js, applies a Caesar-shift transform (keyed on the caller's count argument) to each record's base64 `mark` field, concatenates and base64-decodes the result, then passes the decoded source to the Function constructor with Buffer, require, and process bound as arguments and immediately invokes it. The Function constructor is obtained indirectly via globalThis.constructor.constructor, and the identifiers setTimeout, new Function, Buffer, require, process, try, catch, and clearTimeout are reconstructed by index from a split-token string array (_0x1a2b / _str) to defeat static analysis for Function(/eval(. The declared runtime dependencies python-shell (shell command execution) and axios (HTTP) are not referenced from the readable source and are only reachable from the decoded blob, consistent with hidden shell execution and network I/O against the installer. The data-file cover story, indirect Function acquisition, split-token identifier reconstruction, and unused shell/HTTP dependencies together form a supply-chain dropper that executes attacker-controlled code on any consumer that calls the library's documented API.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
